desc: Explore small cases (N=1,2,3) to understand the game mechanics.
Discover that the sum parity hypothesis fails for samples.
Formulate the game as a state (u, e) where u = unvisited count, e = available extra moves.
Analyze [1,9,2]: game lasts 11 moves, Fennec wins.
Analyze [1,1,3]: game lasts 4 moves, Snuke wins.
Analyze [25,29]: N=2 edge case, Snuke always wins regardless.
Verify hypothesis "count of odd A_i → Fennec if odd, Snuke if even" for N≥3 samples.
Handle N=1,2 as edge cases: N=1 → Fennec, N=2 → Snuke.
Write a brute-force game tree solver for N=3, A_i ≤ 4 to exhaustively determine winners.
Identify the pattern from brute-force results and derive the true rule.
Verify the derived rule against all three samples and edge cases (N=1, N=2).
Implement final solution in Python and test on provided samples.
